articles.title: Scottish Football Podcast - McGinn, McTominay, Robertson: Are Scotland's Legends Undroppable? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Scotland’s first win under Pocognoli and signs of a new identity emerging.
articles.body:
Radio Scotland , · 05 Oct 2026 , · 26 mins

Scotland have their first win under Sebastian Pocognoli, but what did the performance really tell us about the future direction of the national team? Is a clear tactical identity beginning to emerge, and can Scotland become more attacking while keeping their defensive solidity? Charlotte Cohen, Rory Loy and Craig Telfer assess the growing partnership up front, discuss whether Scotland should have scored more goals, and look ahead to the challenge of Slovenia. There’s also a closer look at Andy Robertson after his 100th cap, debate over John McGinn’s role and form, and the big question of where Scott McTominay fits into this evolving Scotland side? 00:02:33 — Is the Pocognoli blueprint emerging? 00:04:51 — Scotland’s finishing problem or a good sign? 00:09:39 — Robertson at 100: where does he rank? 00:14:34 — Can John McGinn rediscover his best form? 00:16:31 — The McTominay selection dilemma 00:19:04 — Are Scotland fans buying into the new approach?

articles.title: The Interview - Olara Otunnu, diplomat: UN cannot be diplomatic ivory tower - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: James Copnall speaks to Olara Otunnu, veteran Ugandan diplomat, about his UN vision
articles.body:
World Service , · 05 Oct 2026 , · 23 mins

“I do not want the United Nations of New York, Geneva or Vienna to be an ivory tower, a diplomatic ivory tower. I want to see the UN not of power and privilege, but the UN of service and impact. That is the UN I want see.” James Copnall speaks to Olara Otunnu, Ugandan diplomat, lawyer and former Foreign Minister. He has spent decades working at the highest levels of international diplomacy. He has also served as a United Nations Under-Secretary-General and Special Representative for Children and Armed Conflict. Now Uganda has formally nominated him for UN Secretary-General, putting him among seven candidates in the running to succeed Antonio Guterres. It is a position widely regarded as the world’s top diplomatic job. Olara Otunnu talks about how he intends to bridge the gap between international politics and the needs of local people around the world. The Interview brings you conversations with people shaping our world, from all over the world. The best interviews from the BBC, including episodes with the UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres, South Africa’s Ambassador to the US Roelf Meyer and the author Maggie O’ Farrell. You can listen on the BBC World Service on Mondays, Wednesdays and Fridays at 0800 GMT. Or you can listen to The Interview as a podcast, out three times a week on BBC Sounds or wherever you get your podcasts. Presenter: James Copnall Producer: Sharon Hemans Editor: Farhana Haider Get in touch with us on email TheInterview@bbc.co.uk and use the hashtag #TheInterviewBBC on social media. articles.title: I warned my son about sextortion. Then scammers targeted his 12-year-old friend.
articles.summary: Whole30 cofounder Melissa Urban shares how scammers targeted her son's 12-year-old friend — and what she wants parents to know about protecting kids from sex...
articles.body:
Melissa Urban may be best known as the cofounder of Whole30 , a popular elimination diet in which you cut out added sugar, dairy, grains, alcohol and more for 30 days, then gradually reintroduce them to see how they impact your health. But her 369,000 followers know that Urban shares more than just healthy eating tips and fitness routines. She's outspoken about supporting women, setting boundaries and protecting your mental health.

These days, however, she's speaking out about a topic that hits close to home: sextortion — specifically, financial sextortion , in which predators, typically pretending to be young girls, message young boys on social media and gaming platforms, convince them to send sexually explicit photos, and then demand money not to publicly release them.

The National Center for Missing & Exploited Children calls sextortion a "growing threat." In 2025, NCMEC received more than 50,000 reports of financially motivated sextortion — an average of 137 per day and a sharp increase from the more than 36,000 reports in 2024. The threat of exposure, which may leave kids feeling isolated and trapped, can have serious consequences . The FBI is aware of more than 20 deaths by suicide resulting from financially motivated sextortion.

Predators often target teens ages 14 to 17 . But with multiple platforms allowing messaging and cash apps to be so easily accessible, even younger boys are being impacted by this crime. That was the case for Urban's son's close friend, who recently became the victim of financial sextortion at just 12 years old.

Urban posted a series of videos on her Instagram last week explaining the harrowing situation involving her son's friend. She helped the family navigate the ordeal and is passionate about raising awareness among parents, especially those who think it couldn't happen to their child. The friend's mom, who wishes to remain anonymous, gave Urban permission to share her son's story here in a conversation with Yahoo's Rachel Grumman Bender.

When my son was around 11 years old, I talked to him about how people can pretend to be someone they're not online, whether it's on Roblox or social media. I told him that some grown-ups do this so they can harm kids. He kept saying to me, "Why would adults do that? Why would they pretend to be kids? It doesn't make any sense." And it's hard to explain to an 11-year-old about predators and grooming.

Then I saw an ESPN article about a young man named Jordan DeMay . He was in his room late at night. He got a DM from a girl [it was actually an extortionist in Nigeria]. They went back and forth. He sent her a [nude] photo. And then "she" began to extort him. Before his parents woke up in the morning, he had sadly died by suicide. And so, reading that and then diving a bit more into it, I realized that this was quite an epidemic, specifically with boys — and athletic ones in particular. [Boys who play sports tend to have a larger online presence, making them easier to find. They're also perceived as having more to lose since a scandal could impact their reputation and recruitment prospects.]

My son really struggled to believe that people did that. But I showed him this article and explained what had happened. We talked about sextortion, what it looks like and the red flags to look out for.

The biggest part of the conversation that I wanted him to understand was this: If anything like this ever happens to you — if you (or a friend) are talking to someone online or you get a message that's weird — end the conversation as soon as possible and come to me . You won't be in trouble. You won't have done anything wrong. I'm not going to be mad at you. You're not going to be punished. As a child, you are not prepared to navigate this. But I will know how to handle this in a way that you won't.

'Hey, this is happening, and I don't know what to do'

Over the summer, my son called me from his friend's house and said, "Mom, my friend just had one of those situations happen on social media." The friend was friended by someone on the app BeReal. She looked like a teenage girl. The extortionists [behind the fake profile] had gone to the trouble of friending this kid's friends on this social media network. So it seemed as though she was a known entity, that she was a safer person to talk to.

The conversation started with, "What are you doing?" "Not much. How about you?" She sent photos of herself, like a selfie, hanging out in bed. And then it escalated to, "Can we send sneaky pictures? Can you send me a picture in your underwear?" His friend kept saying no. He didn't end the conversation, but kept saying no. And finally, this "girl" persuaded him to send a selfie. And he did. He sent a selfie in the mirror, fully clothed in a T-shirt and jeans.

The extortionist took his selfie and used AI or Photoshop to put his face on a naked body. Then they threatened to send it to friends, family and coaches unless he paid them a few hundred dollars. The friend showed my son the interaction and said, "Hey, this is happening, and I don't know what to do."

He was freaked out. So, I got on the phone with him. I asked him to send me screenshots of the messages. Then I explained that this was sextortion and it was illegal. I asked him to preserve the screenshots because on some platforms, when you block someone, the conversation history disappears. I told him to end the conversation immediately and tell his mom. I said, "Your mom and I can definitely keep you safe here."

His mom handled it. She told her son, "You're not in trouble. You didn't do anything wrong. This is a grown-up trying to manipulate a child." They kept the screenshots. They blocked the person. They reported it to the police. The police were able to track down that [the extortionist] originated in Nigeria, so there was very little that they could do. But thankfully, the extortionist never sent out any photos.

I'm not glad we had this as a learning opportunity, but I'm glad it turned out the way it did — because it could have gone so horribly wrong.

Extortionists like these truly behave like a 13-year-old. One of the text messages sent to my son's friend was like, "just hanging out at home, HBU." I don't know a single adult who would text, "how about you" as "HBU," but a kid would. So again, that adult has really infiltrated the language and syntax of teenagers — they really work hard at this. This is often a full-time job.

The extortionist also bombards these kids with message after message after message to add to that sense of fear and urgency [making them more likely to pay them money to make them go away].

While the extortionist could have taken a selfie off a public social media feed, I think the reason they want the child to send the photo themselves is because it's easier to make the child feel culpable. "You sent this to me. You engaged in this interaction. It's your fault that this is happening."

If it's ripped off a school page or social media page, the kid might think, "Well, I had nothing to do with it. My photo was stolen." But in this case, he participates in the exchange. And I think that adds to that sense of guilt and shame for the child.

I thought to myself, But why are they asking children for money? A 12-year-old doesn't have a credit card or a bank account . But what I've read from the FBI and NCMEC is that these kids will often clear out their savings or steal from their parents in order to make this payment, which only furthers that shame and guilt cycle. A lot of my kid's friends have cash apps like Venmo or Zelle or some way for parents to move money back and forth, as well as debit cards for kids like Greenlight.

You tell kids not to talk to strangers on the internet, but social media was literally built for strangers to talk to each other. So that advice is kind of outdated at this point. Parents really have to talk about some of the nuances of internet safety.

I think a lot of parents just aren't aware of the very real risk sextortion poses. It's happening to kids at school. It's happening to your friends' children and kids on sports teams. And it's not just social media, by the way. This is happening on gaming apps like Roblox or Call of Duty . It is happening on message boards like Discord. It's happening on chat apps like WhatsApp or Google Chat.

I read a story about a young girl who was groomed via Spotify because the music app now allows you to send messages. One mom wrote to me after I posted about this, saying, "I just realized my daughter's chess app has a message function."

So it can happen anywhere your child can chat with a stranger on the internet — not just on social media. Even if your kid doesn't have a phone, his friends do. Other family members do. You might have a messaging app on your laptop and not realize that your kid is accessing it. So the most important thing is to have this conversation early and keep having it.

I've heard some comments from parents who are like, "My kid would never. I've talked to them about internet safety." And what I say is this: When it's a child up against an adult dead set on manipulating them, the child is going to lose every time. You cannot expect your kid to be savvy enough at 12, 13, 16 or even 18 when this person's full-time job is manipulating children.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

If you or someone you know is the victim of sextortion, contact your local FBI field office , call 1-800-CALL-FBI, report it online at tips.fbi.gov or contact local law enforcement. If sexually explicit images have been shared, visit the National Center for Missing & Exploited Children's Take It Down tool or Is Your Explicit Content Out There? for potential removal.

If you or someone you know is in suicidal crisis or emotional distress, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988.

articles.title: Cry for help as French-Swiss lake dries up
articles.summary: The picturesque Lac des Brenets between France and Switzerland has dried up after a record-breaking hot summer, leaving locals crying out for help to save th...
articles.body:
The picturesque Lac des Brenets between France and Switzerland has dried up after a record-breaking hot summer, leaving locals crying out for help to save the lake.

Indeed, the words "HELP" and "SOS" have been scratched out in the weeds now flourishing on the exposed lake bed.

The drought has ruined pleasure boat tourism, while some question whether the lake will ever return to enduring full health.

"It's absolutely heartbreaking. It really is emotionally devastating, because it's utter despair: no more lake," said amateur local historian David Favre, who lives in the Swiss village of Les Brenets.

"As children, we used to spend all our summers swimming at the beach, having fun by the water, diving, jumping in and sometimes even fishing," the 76-year-old told AFP.

But "since the last drought in 2018, it's been a disaster. Unfortunately, the lake empties out every couple of years, or soon, perhaps every year," he added, saying he felt the authorities have "completely abandoned" the lake.

The Doubs river rises in the French Jura mountains and normally forms a lake at Les Brenets, where it begins to mark the border between France's Franche-Comte region and Switzerland's Neuchatel canton.

The lake ends at 27-metre-high waterfall, which has now stopped flowing.

The lake has dried up due to a combination of factors, including geological fissures that drain water underground, below-average rainfall and repeated heatwaves.

The months of June, July and August were each the hottest ever recorded in Switzerland since measurements began in 1864.

Every day Yvan Durig, owner and captain of the Lac des Brenets navigation company, measures the level of the remaining basin of water which is shrinking away at the very deepest bit of the lake.

"Normally, we have 25 or 30 metres of depth here," but now there are only nine metres of water left, and within it "the fish are really chock-a-block", he said.

While locals are used to periods of low water, this particular spell is alarming, with the record low of 1906 set to be surpassed imminently.

A task force was set up by French and Swiss authorities in 2022, notably to explore ways of limiting the water draining into the fissures, but has not resulted in decisive action.

"We had to halt boat operations on July 20," said Durig.

"Just imagine: having to stop right in the middle of the season like that. It's unbearable for a company like ours," he said.

"Normally, these are times when we transport 200 to 300 people a day," said Durig.

Pontoons and dozens of boats lie stranded on the dry lake bed.

The water level monitoring station for the lake is now so far out of the remaining basin that Durig does the measurements manually.

The water line is dropping around 20 to 22 centimetres a day.

On October 1, it fell to an elevation of 735.34 metres above sea level -- fully 14.66 metres below where it should be.

Within days, it is expected to surpass the 1906 record drop of 15.35 metres.

A tiny stream now trickles through the weeds on the lake bed.

Maxime Fallet, who works at a Doubs riverboat excursion company, fears the lake is "destined to disappear", for lack of a plan to save it.

"The atmosphere in Les Brenets these days, when talk turns to the Doubs, is often tinged with a certain sadness, a melancholy at the thought that we could lose this lake -- a lake that has been part of the soul of Les Brenets for generations," he told AFP.

"We must take action -- indeed, be proactive -- and seal the lakebed," he said.

"But this can no longer take years. That is simply not an option anymore."

articles.title: Girl, 12, fatally shot in US during 'dispute over parking space'
articles.summary: Police in Baltimore have said the young girl was not a target of the shooting but was caught in the crossfire.
articles.body:
A 12-year-old girl was killed in Baltimore over the weekend during an apparent disagreement over a parking space, police in the US city said.

The girl was caught in the crossfire of bullets between two men who police said were allegedly fighting over a parking space in a park where children were playing American football.

In addition to the young girl, a woman was also found with gunshot wounds when police arrived on the scene. Two men also visited area hospitals for injuries believed to be related to the shooting, police said.

Police are now searching for at least two suspects, Baltimore Police Commissioner Richard Worley said at a news conference. No arrests have been made.

"What we know is there was some type of argument between two cowards," Worley said. "They both opened fire on each other. In the crossfire, a 12-year-old little girl, who was probably down there watching football, was shot and killed."

Worley said the girl, who police have not named, was not a target of the shooting.

The girl was pronounced dead in hospital. The other three individuals who were injured have non-life-threatening injuries, Worley said.

The incident happened after 18:00 EDT (23:00 BST) on Saturday.

Authorities are still investigating the shooting and have asked any witnesses to bring information to police.

It remains unclear how many shots were fired, Worley said.

"Two grown men got into an argument, and now a 12-year-old is gone," Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott said at the news conference.

"We never should have to say something like that. What happened out here today is one of the most disgusting things I've ever seen in my life."

articles.title: Plantão Psicológico gratuito da Unifor acolhe casais e famílias em Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: Serviço da Universidade de Fortaleza oferece atendimento psicológico por ordem de chegada e amplia o acesso da população ao cuidado em saúde mental
articles.summary: Serviço da Universidade de Fortaleza oferece atendimento psicológico por ordem de chegada e amplia o acesso da população ao cuidado em saúde mental
articles.body:
Os atendimentos ocorrem no Núcleo de Atenção Médica Integrada (NAMI) — Foto: Getty Images

Conflitos conjugais, dificuldades nas relações familiares, momentos de crise e situações de sofrimento emocional podem fazer parte da trajetória de diferentes pessoas e famílias. Para oferecer um espaço de acolhimento e escuta à população, a Universidade de Fortaleza, instituição mantida pela Fundação Edson Queiroz , disponibiliza o Plantão Psicológico , serviço gratuito de atendimento psicológico emergencial que também contempla .

A proposta do serviço, conduzido pelo Curso de Psicologia , é oferecer um espaço de acolhimento para pessoas que buscam espontaneamente atendimento psicológico diante de situações emergenciais. Pioneiro entre as instituições de ensino superior no atendimento psicológico a casais e famílias em formato de plantão , o serviço possibilita um acesso direto ao cuidado psicológico, sem depender de encaminhamentos prévios. O atendimento é realizado de forma espontânea e por ordem de chegada, de acordo com o número de senhas disponíveis . O serviço funciona, neste semestre, até o dia 27 de novembro, com três senhas por turno, por semana.

O Plantão Psicológico está localizado no 2º andar do Serviço de Psicologia Aplicada (SPA), no NAMI, na Rua Maramaldo Campelo, nº 50, no bairro Edson Queiroz, em Fortaleza.

Como serviço de promoção de saúde, o plantão psicológico com casais e famílias pode colaborar como espaço de acolhimento e escuta na redução do estresse, da ansiedade e proporcionar suporte ao enfrentamento das crises conjugais e familiares .

A iniciativa também pode auxiliar como espaço de acolhimento e compreensão das necessidades e demandas da população no que se refere à atenção básica em saúde mental e à assistência psicossocial, somando informações e fornecendo dados para a elaboração de políticas públicas nessas redes de proteção social.

Para a Universidade de Fortaleza, o serviço representa uma importante estratégia clínica voltada para a comunidade, favorecendo o acesso da população a um serviço gratuito de saúde e possibilitando a inclusão terapêutica de casais e famílias vulneráveis, que podem enfrentar seus conflitos e crises com mais esse recurso externo.

A iniciativa também possui relevância para a formação acadêmica. Para o curso de graduação em Psicologia, o projeto pode se constituir como uma atividade de extensão e pesquisa, favorecendo o campo de conhecimento e o desenvolvimento de novas pesquisas na área. Para os estudantes, o contato com esse público contribui para a preparação dos futuros profissionais para atuar em contextos que exigem uma maior compreensão de situações graves ou críticas envolvendo casais e famílias.

De acordo com o coordenador da iniciativa, Álvaro Rebouças , o aprimoramento do Plantão Psicológico passa pela necessidade de acompanhar as transformações nas configurações conjugais e familiares e pelas demandas que ainda não chegam aos serviços de Psicologia.

“Em 2020 não foi percebida a chegada de novas demandas, mas há uma série de formas de ser casal e ser família que não chegaram aos atendimentos do plantão psicológico, como: as famílias em situação de rua (HONORATO e OLIVEIRA, 2020), as famílias homossexuais (NASCIMENTO e MAI, 2016), as uniões poliafetivas (GESSE, 2020), as famílias poliamorosas (VILLA MONSALVE, RAMÍREZ HERRERA e ZAPATA ARIAS, 2016), as famílias transgêneros (CARDIN e VIEIRA, 2019) e outras.”

Nesse sentido, segundo Rebouças, o serviço pode ampliar sua capacidade de acolhimento diante das transformações sociais e familiares:

“Nesse sentido, o plantão psicológico com casais e famílias pode se transformar no espaço de recebimento das demandas das novas e novíssimas configurações conjugais e familiares em busca de alcançar mudanças pretendidas ou apenas para compreender as questões que estão vivendo.”

A necessidade de transformação também envolve os próprios modelos de atendimento. “Certamente, diante das novas e novíssimas demandas, precisarão ser desenvolvidas, adaptadas ou buscadas novas formas de modelos de apoio e de atendimento. O plantão com casais e famílias como espaço de acolhimento e escuta dever se transformar conforme refaz sua finalidade.”

Segunda-feira pela manhã: a partir das 8h — atendimento individual, a partir de 13 anos.

Terça-feira à tarde: atendimento individual, a partir das 14h — a partir de 12 anos.

Quinta-feira à tarde: atendimento individual, a partir das 14h — a partir de 12 anos.

Sexta-feira à tarde: atendimento para casais e famílias, a partir das 14h.

Para participar do atendimento, é necessário ter prontuário no NAMI e apresentar os seguintes documentos: RG, CNH ou CIN; Cartão Nacional de Saúde (CNS); CPF; Certidão de Nascimento, para crianças que não possuem RG; comprovante de endereço e e-mail.

R. Maramaldo Campelo, nº 50 - Edson Queiroz

articles.title: Oeste do Pará elege dois deputados federais e quatro estaduais; veja lista e suplentes | G1
articles.standfirst: Região assegurou representação na Câmara dos Deputados e na Alepa para a legislatura de 2027. Levantamento também detalha os nomes que ficaram na suplência.
articles.summary: Região assegurou representação na Câmara dos Deputados e na Alepa para a legislatura de 2027. Levantamento também detalha os nomes que ficaram na suplência.
articles.body:
Montagem reúne Renata Fonseca, Maria do Carmo, JK do Povão e Ângelo Ferrari, deputados estaduais eleitos pelo oeste do Pará para a Alepa. — Foto: Redes Sociais

O oeste do Pará elegeu seis representantes para o Poder Legislativo no primeiro turno das Eleições 2026, realizado neste domingo (4). Com o resultado oficial consolidado pela Justiça Eleitoral, lideranças políticas da região garantiram duas cadeiras na Câmara dos Deputados, em Brasília, e quatro vagas na Assembleia Legislativa do Estado do Pará (Alepa), em Belém.

Entre os eleitos estão nomes com domicílio eleitoral concentrado nos municípios de Santarém e Oriximiná, que mobilizaram expressiva votação no Baixo Amazonas e na Calha Norte.

Para o Congresso Nacional, o deputado federal reeleito Júnior Ferrari (PSD) renovou o mandato após receber 213.645 votos em todo o estado. Ele figurou entre os mais votados da bancada paraense.

A segunda vaga federal da região ficou com o deputado Airton Faleiro (PT), que tem base política em Santarém e somou 90.181 votos válidos. Ambos integrarão o grupo de 17 parlamentares que representarão o Pará na Câmara a partir do próximo ano.

Na disputa pelas 41 vagas da Alepa, o deputado estadual reeleito Ângelo Ferrari (União Brasil) assegurou a permanência no parlamento estadual com a soma de 77.454 votos. O parlamentar mantém forte atuação nos municípios da Calha Norte.

Também por Oriximiná, a servidora pública Renata Fonseca (PL) garantiu vaga na Alepa ao alcançar 75.841 votos em sua primeira eleição para o legislativo paraense .

O colégio eleitoral de Santarém conquistou outras duas vagas estaduais. O vereador JK do Povão (PL) garantiu assento na Alepa ao atingir 69.719 votos no Pará, enquanto a ex-prefeita santarena Maria do Carmo (PT) confirmou seu retorno ao legislativo estadual com 50.558 votos válidos.

A apuração regional também definiu a ordem dos candidatos que ficaram na suplência das bancadas. Na disputa pela Câmara dos Deputados, Henderson Pinto (União Brasil) obteve 98.847 votos, seguido por Adriana Almeida (MDB), com 88.147 votos, Chapadinha (Podemos), com 14.180 votos, e Biga (PT), que alcançou 11.281 votos.

Já na corrida pelas cadeiras da Alepa, o primeiro suplente da região foi João Pingarilho (MDB), com 45.770 votos, acompanhado pelo ex-prefeito Nélio Aguiar (União Brasil), que somou 36.856 votos. Também figuram na lista Josué Paiva (Avante, 31.054 votos), Dayan Rocha (Avante, 17.219 votos), Auricélia Arapiun (PSOL, 10.601 votos), Adriana Falconeri (União Brasil, 4.902 votos) e Elielton Lira (PDT, 3.455 votos).

Conforme o calendário do Tribunal Regional Eleitoral do Pará (TRE-PA), os candidatos eleitos serão diplomados em sessão solene até o mês de dezembro. Já o início oficial dos trabalhos legislativos para o mandato de quatro anos está marcado para 1º de fevereiro de 2027 .

articles.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vence em 8 das 9 cidades da Baixada Santista | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato do PL venceu em oito municípios da região, enquanto o petista ganhou apenas em Cubatão no 1º turno. As maiores vantagens foram registradas em Praia Grande e Bertioga.
articles.summary: Flávio Bolsonaro liderou a votação na Baixada Santista com vitórias em Praia Grande e Bertioga, enquanto Lula foi o mais votado apenas no município de Cubatão.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro ao chegar para votar em sua seção eleitoral no Rio de Janeiro — Foto: Lucas Landau/AP

O candidato à presidência Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) foi o mais votado no 1º turno nas eleições na Baixada Santista. Dos nove municípios, Flávio venceu em oito . Já o candidato à reeleição, Lula (PT), venceu apenas em Cubatão.

As eleições gerais de 2026 aconteceram neste domingo (4), das 8h às 17h. Com 100% das urnas apuradas, Flávio Bolsonaro teve 47,03% dos votos válidos, enquanto Lula ficou com 45,16% .

Na Baixada Santista, Flávio obteve vantagem sobre Lula na maioria dos municípios. Praia Grande (SP) foi a cidade onde o candidato teve a maior vantagem percentual sobre o petista, com 54,15% dos votos, contra 36,36% de Lula.

Já em Cubatão, único município da região onde o petista venceu, Lula obteve 46,27% dos votos, contra 44,40% de Flávio Bolsonaro.

articles.title: Maior eleição da história: veja como foi o domingo de votação | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 158,7 milhões de pessoas aptas a votar, pleito reuniu diferentes gerações nas urnas, do primeiro voto aos eleitores com mais de 90 anos.
articles.summary: Com 158,7 milhões de pessoas aptas a votar, pleito reuniu diferentes gerações nas urnas, do primeiro voto aos eleitores com mais de 90 anos.
articles.body:
As Eleições 2026 são as maiores da história em número de eleitores, com 158 milhões de pessoas aptas a votar em todo o país.

O eleitorado é formado principalmente por mulheres e pessoas mais velhas, mas a votação reúne brasileiros de diferentes idades, perfis e opiniões. O número mostra a dimensão de uma eleição realizada em um país com mais de 200 milhões de habitantes.

Em diferentes regiões do Brasil, os eleitores foram às urnas neste domingo (4) para participar do processo eleitoral. Houve desde pessoas que votaram pela primeira vez até eleitores com mais de 90 anos.

Aos 96 anos, o ex-presidente José Sarney votou em São Luís, acompanhado de um neto. Já em Praia Grande, no litoral de São Paulo, o mesário Hermenegildo, também de 96 anos, voltou a trabalhar em uma eleição.

“Na idade avançada, mas eu ainda posso contribuir, né, para a democracia”, disse.

Entre os eleitores que participaram da votação está Monique, de 16 anos, que votou pela primeira vez. Ela contou que ficou nervosa antes de entrar na cabine, mas conseguiu concluir a votação.

“Fiquei nervosa por não saber, mas aí na hora deu tudo certo”, afirmou.

A dimensão do eleitorado também se refletiu nas diferentes formas encontradas pelos brasileiros para chegar aos locais de votação.

Na maior parte das capitais, houve transporte público gratuito, com passe livre em ônibus, trens e metrôs. Em Urânia, no interior de São Paulo, um casal decidiu ir votar de charrete.

Em Fortaleza, Francisco, que tem dificuldade de locomoção, elogiou a acessibilidade do local de votação.

“Tem acesso, tem rampa, não tive dificuldade nenhuma. Ótimo local”, afirmou.

Em outros pontos do país, eleitores enfrentaram situações como apagões. Mesmo assim, a votação não foi interrompida porque as urnas eletrônicas possuem bateria própria.

Pela primeira vez, o ato de votar também serviu oficialmente como prova de vida para aposentados e pensionistas do INSS.

A medida foi lembrada por eleitores que destacaram a praticidade de realizar o procedimento durante a votação.

“É um comprovante de vida e é muito mais prático. Vim aqui votar, tem lá com o INSS aquela burocracia toda”, disse um eleitor.

articles.title: Luiza Erundina e Eduarda Campopiano: conheça a deputada eleita mais velha e a mais jovem da Alesp | G1
articles.standfirst: Com 169.567 votos, Erundina vai retornar à Alesp em 2027, após 40 anos. Eduarda foi a deputada mais votada na Alesp neste ano: 1.956.238.
articles.summary: Com 169.567 votos, Erundina vai retornar à Alesp em 2027, após 40 anos. Eduarda foi a deputada mais votada na Alesp neste ano: 1.956.238.
articles.body:
As deputadas estaduais eleitas em SP Luiza Erundina (PSOL) e Eduarda Campopiano (PL) — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

Eleitas neste domingo (4), Luiza Erundina (PSOL), de 91 anos, e Eduarda Campopiano (PL), de 23, serão as deputadas mais idosa e mais jovem da Assembleia Legislativa do estado de São Paulo (Alesp) a partir da próxima Legislatura.

A experiente Erundina foi eleita, em 1988, a primeira prefeita da capital paulista. Está em seu sétimo mandato consecutivo como parlamentar na Câmara dos Deputados. Com 169.567 votos, vai retornar à Alesp em 2027, após 40 anos.

Natural de Uiraúna, no Sertão da Paraíba, Erundina é assistente social formada pela UFPB. Após concluir um mestrado em Ciências Sociais em São Paulo, ela ingressaria como professora no Departamento de Ciências Sociais da UFPB, no início da década de 1970, mas teve o curso de sua trajetória docente alterado por causa da sua atuação como militante da causa camponesa.

Considerada uma ameaça ao regime militar, Luiza teve seu ingresso como professora da instituição vetado pelos militares e teve que se mudar para São Paulo por força da perseguição. Lá, a paraibana construiu sua carreira política, primeiro como vereadora, depois como deputada estadual, prefeita e deputada federal.

Eduarda, por sua vez, é vereadora em Praia Grande, no litoral paulista, e vai estrear no Legislativo paulista como a candidata mais votada para a Alesp nas eleições de 2026, com 1.956.238 votos. A jovem parlamentar ganhou projeção nas redes sociais com pautas conservadoras e alinhadas ao bolsonarismo.

A votação é a segunda maior da história do estado, atrás apenas dos cerca de 2 milhões de votos recebidos em 2018 pela advogada Janaína Paschoal, hoje vereadora na capital paulista pelo PP.

Nascida em Campinas em 22 de julho de 2003, Eduarda é influenciadora digital e ingressou na política eleitoral em 2024. Naquele ano, foi eleita vereadora de Praia Grande, no litoral paulista, com 3.583 votos, tornando-se a parlamentar mais jovem da história recente da Câmara Municipal da cidade ao tomar posse aos 21 anos.

Filiada ao Partido Liberal, a deputada eleita construiu sua campanha estadual fortemente apoiada na comunicação digital. Durante a disputa de 2026, seus conteúdos foram direcionados principalmente ao eleitorado conservador, com defesa da família tradicional, da vida desde a concepção e da presença de princípios cristãos na política. Também se posicionou contra pautas progressistas, o feminismo contemporâneo e o que classifica como "cultura woke".

A disputa em São Paulo teve cerca de 23,2 milhões de votos válidos e 3 milhões de votos brancos e nulos. As abstenções bateram recorde: mais de 7,6 milhões de pessoas deixaram de comparecer às urnas, o equivalente a aproximadamente 22,5% dos 34,1 milhões de eleitores aptos a votar no estado.

O PL foi o principal vencedor da disputa para a Assembleia Legislativa, elegendo 28 deputados estaduais, quase um terço das cadeiras da Casa. A legenda foi impulsionada pela votação recorde de Eduarda Campopiano, que recebeu 1,95 milhão de votos e se tornou a candidata mais votada da eleição (veja lista completa abaixo) .

O resultado consolidou a força do campo político liderado pelo governador reeleito Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos). Somadas ao PL, as bancadas do PSD, União Brasil, Podemos, PP, Republicanos e MDB elegeram 63 dos 94 deputados estaduais, garantindo ao Palácio dos Bandeirantes uma base confortável para aprovar projetos e conduzir a agenda do governo nos próximos quatro anos

Na oposição, o PT elegeu a segunda maior bancada da Alesp. Impulsionado pela expressiva votação de Eduardo Suplicy, segundo deputado estadual mais votado do estado, o partido elegeu 15 parlamentares, mas perdeu duas cadeiras em relação à composição da legislatura que se encerra.

Já o PSOL consolidou-se como a terceira força da Assembleia e ampliou sua presença ao eleger nove deputados estaduais.

articles.title: Saltinho tem maior percentual de votos para Flávio e Tarcísio em SP; Itapura é destaque de Lula e Haddad | G1
articles.standfirst: Na região de Piracicaba, Flávio teve 78,71% e Tarcísio, 86,22% em Saltinho; na divisa com Mato Grosso do Sul, Lula chegou a 62,57% e Haddad, a 60,53%.
articles.summary: Na região de Piracicaba, Flávio teve 78,71% e Tarcísio, 86,22% em Saltinho; na divisa com Mato Grosso do Sul, Lula chegou a 62,57% e Haddad, a 60,53%.
articles.body:
Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) durante a Festa do Peão de Barreto — Foto: Érico Andrade/g1

O mapa da votação no estado de São Paulo mostra dois municípios que se destacaram pelos percentuais obtidos pelos candidatos que disputaram o segundo turno para presidente e governador neste domingo (4).

Saltinho , na Região Metropolitana de Piracicaba, teve os maiores percentuais de votação para Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) e Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) . Já Itapura , no extremo noroeste do estado e na divisa com Mato Grosso do Sul, foi onde Lula (PT) e Fernando Haddad (PT) tiveram seus melhores desempenhos proporcionais.

Na disputa pelo governo de São Paulo, Tarcísio teve um desempenho ainda maior no município. O governador reeleito recebeu 86,22% dos votos, ou 4.669 votos, também o maior percentual registrado por ele entre as cidades paulistas.

O resultado percentual de Flávio Bolsonaro em Saltinho foi superior ao obtido por seu pai, Jair Bolsonaro (PL), no primeiro turno da eleição presidencial de 2022. Naquele ano, Bolsonaro recebeu 75,77% dos votos no município, o equivalente a 4.143 votos. Lula teve 16,62%, com 909 votos.

Saltinho tem pouco mais de 8 mil habitantes e está localizada na Região Metropolitana de Piracicaba, a cerca de 180 km da capital paulista. A origem do município está ligada à expansão agrícola da região de Piracicaba e à influência da imigração italiana.

Lula e Fernando Haddad, em Brasília. — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

Do outro lado do mapa eleitoral, Itapura foi o município onde Lula e Haddad tiveram os maiores percentuais de votação no estado de São Paulo.

Com 3.979 habitantes, segundo os dados oficiais do Censo do IBGE, o município tem população estimada em aproximadamente 3.990 habitantes nas estimativas mais recentes do instituto. Itapura fica na divisa de São Paulo com Mato Grosso do Sul.

Na disputa presidencial, Lula recebeu 62,57% dos votos válidos na cidade, o equivalente a 1.583 votos. Foi o maior percentual alcançado pelo presidente entre os municípios paulistas.

Na eleição para o governo de São Paulo, Haddad também teve em Itapura seu melhor desempenho proporcional. O candidato recebeu 60,53% dos votos, ou 1.400 votos.

Itapura foi ainda uma das seis cidades paulistas em que Haddad terminou à frente de Tarcísio na disputa pelo governo.

Além dela, o petista venceu em Coronel Macedo, Sandovalina, Euclides da Cunha Paulista, Francisco Morato e Diadema. Nas outras 639 das 645 cidades paulistas, Tarcísio terminou à frente de Haddad.

O governador reeleito de São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas — Foto: Rafael Peixoto/g1

Tarcísio de Freitas foi reeleito governador de São Paulo neste domingo (4) , derrotando Haddad pela segunda vez consecutiva em uma eleição estadual. A vitória foi confirmada às 19h39, quando 90% das urnas já haviam sido apuradas.

Com 99,91% das urnas apuradas, Tarcísio tinha 14.477.619 votos, superando os 13.480.643 votos recebidos no segundo turno de 2022. O resultado estabeleceu um novo recorde de votação para um candidato ao governo de São Paulo.

A distribuição dos votos também foi diferente da registrada em 2022. Naquela eleição, Tarcísio venceu em 500 cidades, enquanto Haddad ganhou em 91 municípios, incluindo a capital paulista. Neste ano, Tarcísio venceu em 639 cidades e Haddad em apenas seis.

articles.standfirst: O órgão declarou que trabalhou em estreita cooperação com autoridades brasileiras para tratar das questões de segurança.
articles.summary: O Consulado dos EUA em Porto Alegre e demais unidades no Brasil retomaram os atendimentos nesta segunda-feira (5) após suspensão por alerta de segurança.
articles.body:
Consulado dos EUA em Porto Alegre suspende serviços após 'alerta de segurança' — Foto: Mateus Bruxel/Agência RBS

O Consulado dos Estados Unidos em Porto Alegre e as demais representações diplomáticas do país no Brasil retomaram os atendimentos nesta segunda-feira (05) após a suspensão dos serviços anunciada na sexta (02).

De acordo com um porta-voz do Departamento de Estado, foi emitido pelo governo americano um alerta de segurança, motivo para a paralisação do atendimento . Não há detalhe sobre o que seria a questão de segurança.

O órgão declarou que trabalhou em estreita cooperação com autoridades brasileiras para tratar das questões de segurança.

"A Administração Trump não tem prioridade maior do que a segurança e a proteção dos cidadãos americanos. A Embaixada dos EUA e seus Consulados no Brasil retomarão as operações normais na segunda-feira, 5 de outubro, incluindo os serviços consulares. Continuaremos a fornecer, de forma proativa, informações oportunas sobre segurança e proteção aos cidadãos americanos no Brasil, enquanto seguimos trabalhando com nossos parceiros brasileiros em questões de segurança", afirmou o porta-voz do Departamento de Estado.

Segundo o porta-voz, o governo utiliza regularmente o sistema de mensagens STEP para enviar alertas e informar os cidadãos americanos sobre ameaças, eventos e mudanças relevantes no contexto local.

A assessoria de imprensa do Consulado-Geral dos EUA em Porto Alegre também informou que os solicitantes de visto "foram avisados individualmente sobre o cancelamento das entrevistas. Instruções sobre como reagendar a entrevista serão enviadas diretamente aos solicitantes".

articles.title: Remembering the British Home Children sent to Canada all alone
articles.summary: Many of those sent away under the British Home Children migration scheme sailed via Liverpool.
articles.body:
When 10-year-old Rose Shapcott and her brother Fred, 14, were orphaned and put into a Barnardo's children's home in 1891, little did they know they would end up being separated and sent thousands of miles away across the Atlantic.

The siblings were sent to Canada as part of the British Home Children child migration programme, which saw about 100,000 impoverished children from Britain sent to overseas colonies including Canada, between 1869 and the 1940s.

These children were separated from their families and sent off to Canada as a source of cheap labour, often suffering mistreatment at the hands of those who took them in, said Rose's great grandson Malcolm Farrow.

Farrow said Fred was sent to Saskatchewan first and then Rose asked to be sent over when she was 17, thinking they would be reunited.

Instead, she was sent thousands of miles away to Peterborough in Ontario and went on to have "a very sad life", Farrow revealed.

Rose ended up getting married but Fred managed to get her back to England as he was concerned about her.

She had a baby boy illegitimately, but he was put into care due to having a disability. At one point, Rose was admitted to an asylum in England when she began struggling with her mental health, Farrow explained.

Eventually, she returned to her husband in Canada, without her son, and died in 1916.

Farrow is a board member at the Home Children Canada charity, which raises awareness of the young child migrants, some of whom died in childhood.

Their work has included locating and documenting burial sites across Canada, including a mass grave of 76 British Home Children in Etobicoke, Ontario - and erecting a monument in their honour.

In another case, George Roberts was 15 when he was sent to Canada on a ship called the Corsican, which sailed out of the Albert Dock in 1913.

According to Simon Roberts - whom George was the great uncle of - he was born out of wedlock in Liverpool in 1897. After his mother moved to London to escape the shame, he was put into care when she began struggling to provide for him and his older brother.

Roberts said being a bit older, his uncle was "one of the luckier ones", but many children endured horrific experiences.

He said "the problem was that, although I think there were good intentions in the UK, there was no inspection process or supervision in Canada".

Roberts said some of the children died and the abuse some faced included being "put into fields in the middle of a Canadian winter with no shoes, with no boots, and told to work the fields".

Roberts said he was "extremely disappointed to discover that there is no memorial to the journeys undertaken by these children in the country from which they were sent".

He said the Home Children Canada charity was "trying to get Liverpool City Council to allow us to put a memorial up to remember these poor lonely little children, many of which were treated horrifically in their short lives".

The proposed memorial shows a young boy and girl dressed ready to get on the boat, each holding a little suitcase, and looking out across the Mersey.

The Home Children Canada charity said it would be willing to pay for the statue but it needs permission to erect it in the city.

Sheila Dodd, also a descendant of one of the British Home Children, said the charity believed that 10-15% of all British Home Children came from the Liverpool area, with at least six sending agencies and homes based in the city.

Dodd said her grandmother Heather McGrath and her grandmother's brother James were sent to Canada via Liverpool in 1930 and 1927 respectively.

She said she was able to speak to her grandmother, who told her about "her terrible experiences".

Dodd said she hoped the memorial could be erected in Liverpool so she and other descendants could visit it as a place of pilgrimage.

The BBC has approached Liverpool City Council for comment.

articles.title: BT agrees rescue deal to buy broadband operator TalkTalk
articles.summary: The takeover still needs to be approved by the regulator, but would give certainty to TalkTalk's millions of customers
articles.body:
The UK's biggest broadband provider, BT, has agreed to buy rival operator TalkTalk to save the company from collapse .

The takeover would end of months of speculation over the future of TalkTalk and mean services for its millions of customers will continue as normal.

BT boss Alison Kirkby said it provided "a safety net" for TalkTalk customers. The administrator, Alvarez & Marsal, said it also provided certainty for TalkTalk's 900 staff based in Salford, Greater Manchester.

However, Virgin Media called it a "stitch-up" which allows BT to "tighten its grip" over the market. The government has given itself the power to have the final say on the deal, citing its importance to vital public services.

TalkTalk has 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers across the UK.

BT's Kirkby told the BBC's Today programme: "Two and a half million customers, including vulnerable households, and key emergency services might have lost their services if Talk Talk had failed, which it was on track to do.

"So BT stepped in as we were the only viable option to take the business forward."

Ernest Doku from comparison website Uswitch said the deal means "nothing changes today".

"Your broadband and landline carry on as normal, and there is nothing you need to do right now," he added.

However, he said that BT should explain "quickly and plainly what this means for contracts, prices and service in the future, so nobody is left guessing".

The regulator, Ofcom, says broadband customers should have the right to leave a contract without an exit fee if a new owner puts the price up beyond what was in the contract.

TalkTalk began as a challenger to BT in the broadband market. It was listed on the London Stock Exchange, but was taken over by private equity in 2021.

Since then, the firm has built up debt while losing customers, leaving it unable to pay some of those it owes money to.

Despite this, TalkTalk remained the fourth biggest broadband provider in the UK, with 6.6% of customers, during the March to June period of this year, according to figures from analytic firm Opensignal.

BT has 32.5% of customers, Sky 19.9%, and Virgin Media 19.1%.

Rivals who were beaten to the deal by BT have said it will be bad for consumers.

Tom O'Hagan, a former TalkTalk executive who was leading a takeover bid for the firm, told the BBC he was worried about "reduced choice and potentially an increase in price for consumers and for businesses" because of the BT deal.

He added that he was particularly concerned about competition in the wholesale market, where TalkTalk's subsidiary PXC was BT's main rival.

Virgin Media, which has also reportedly tried to buy TalkTalk in the past, said the BT takeover has "all the characteristics of a stitch-up masked as a rescue deal in the public interest".

It added that the purchase means BT can "roll its tanks over competition and further tighten its grip on the market. The logic simply doesn't add up."

The Competition Markets Authority (CMA) will need to approve the takeover, which would give BT greater power over the broadband market.

Tom Smith, a competition lawyer and former legal director at the CMA, said the regulator will be balancing that concern with other considerations.

"When the CMA looks at it, it will look at what would have happened if the deal wasn't going through," he told the BBC.

"If TalkTalk would have exited the market, for example, then really any deal is better than TalkTalk exiting, but then there might be alternative bidders as well that would have been less anticompetitive."

However, the Department of Culture, Media, and Sport (DCMS) has given itself the power to make the final decision on the deal in the name of the public interest once the CMA has made its report.

DCMS has given the CMA until 19 October to deliver its verdict.

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy said: "Phone and broadband services are vital national infrastructure.

"If TalkTalk services fail, there is a genuine risk to life and public services – including to hospitals, schools and emergency care. These are unprecedented circumstances that require action now."

BT has said it welcomed the intervention and would "work constructively with the government and the CMA during their review".

Judith Mackenzie, a partner at investment manager Downing, told the BBC that broadband was "not a regulated industry, unlike electricity and water, but it's also very important to business users and ourselves, consumers".

"It's almost like a commodity now, broadband," she added.

BT has said it will cost the firm £400m to buy TalkTalk out of administration.

This includes the purchase price, fees, TalkTalk's expected £60m loss for this year, and BT effectively writing off the £100m TalkTalk owes BT's Openreach business.

TalkTalk has £1.5bn of debt and made a £100m loss last year.

articles.title: Coast Guard personnel exchange gunfire with shooters across US-Mexico border
articles.summary: Coast Guard personnel returned fire after shots came from the Mexican side of the southern border, prompting a massive troop deployment to the region.
articles.body: Coast Guard personnel exchanged gunfire with people on the Mexican side of the border, an encounter the U.S. military later cited as an example of increased illegal activity as hundreds of U.S. troops and their equipment were repositioned to Texas’ Rio Grande Valley and 500 Mexican Army and National Guard personnel were deployed to its side of the border. Coast Guard personnel were intercepting migrants crossing the Rio Grande while working with other federal agencies when the initial gunshots came from the Mexican side of the border. Coast Guard personnel then returned fire, officials said on Friday, according to Stars and Stripes. The exchange happened on Sept. 26 while federal agencies conducted joint operations near Garceno, a small town along the border in Starr County, Texas. DHS SENDS OMINOUS WARNING AS MIGRANT CARAVAN HEADS TOWARD US-MEXICO BORDER FROM HONDURAS The Coast Guard said it was investigating the incident alongside federal partners. It is unclear who fired the initial shots. "No injuries to Coast Guard or other personnel were reported, and no damage to Coast Guard assets or equipment was reported," the Coast Guard said. U.S. Ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson said the embassy "is helping to coordinate with Mexican forces that are being deployed in the border area where shots were fired against elements of the United States Coast Guard." "Mexican military commanders will communicate directly with the U.S. forces deployed. Together, we intend to patrol both sides of our shared border, protect our communities and disrupt the operations of criminal and terrorist organizations. Any threat from criminal or terrorist elements on either side of the border will be addressed swiftly," he added. The Coast Guard launched Operation River Wall in October 2025, deploying additional personnel, boats and other assets to patrol the river between the U.S. and Mexico. The Coast Guard said its forces would focus on approximately 260 miles of the Rio Grande along the U.S.-Mexico border. It was working closely with Border Patrol, the Pentagon and the Texas Military Department "to secure the border, disrupt illicit activity and protect the American people," the Coast Guard said, according to Stars and Stripes. "We will continue to leverage a layered, integrated approach to control, secure and defend the border that strengthens our collective ability to counter illicit activity and safeguard our personnel and the communities we serve," the Coast Guard said. TRUMP ADMIN'S LIST OF US-DESIGNATED 'FOREIGN TERRORIST' GROUPS IN LATIN AMERICA EXPANDS TO 21 CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The U.S. military said on Friday it had deployed hundreds of troops and their equipment to the Rio Grande Valley as part of planned preparations to address "historically observed seasonal increases in attempted illegal activity." "The Sept. 26 Coast Guard encounter is an example of this uptick in illegal activity," the Joint Task Force-Southern Border said in a statement.

articles.title: ‘Transnational repression’: FBI arrests California woman accused of spying on Taiwan president’s family for China
articles.summary: The FBI has arrested a California woman at Los Angeles International Airport as she was preparing to leave the United States for China, accusing her of
articles.body: The FBI has arrested a California woman at Los Angeles International Airport as she was preparing to leave the United States for China, accusing her of acting as an unregistered agent for Beijing and surveilling the family of Taiwan President Lai Ching-te.Wanying Zhang, also known as Heather, 34, was arrested on Sunday and charged with acting as an unregistered foreign agent, according to the FBI and US authorities. Investigators allege that Zhang gathered photographs, videos and vehicle licence plate information about Lai’s son and his family and passed the material to Chinese officials.The arrest comes against the backdrop of intensifying tensions between Beijing and Taipei, with China continuing to claim Taiwan as part of its territory and Lai taking a firm position on the island’s separate political identity.According to the Justice Department, Zhang travelled to Seattle in 2025 at the direction of Chinese officials and subsequently sent them photographs, videos and licence plate information relating to the Taiwanese president’s son and his family.The FBI said Zhang used methods intended to avoid detection while carrying out the alleged surveillance and did not notify US authorities that she was acting on behalf of a foreign government.Bill Essayli, first assistant US attorney for the Central District of California, announced the arrest and said Zhang had been working for China without registering as a foreign agent as required under US law.Zhang was detained at Los Angeles International Airport shortly before she was due to board a flight to China. She is scheduled to appear in federal court in Los Angeles on Monday.It was not immediately clear whether Zhang had an attorney representing her. Her nationality was also not immediately known.Taiwan calls alleged surveillance ‘transnational repression’Taiwan's Presidential Office confirmed that relatives of Lai were targeted but did not specify whether the president's son was the person under surveillance.Taiwanese officials described the alleged operation as an example of Beijing extending pressure beyond its borders to target people connected to the island's leadership.“This is a classic case of transnational repression,” Presidential Office spokesperson Karen Kuo said in a statement.“Taiwan condemns in the strongest terms such barbaric acts — which disregard human rights and national sovereignty and aim to suppress, threaten, or even harm individuals advocating for freedom and democracy or their families — as such behavior should not be tolerated in the civilized world,” Kuo said.The Chinese Embassy in Washington did not immediately respond to requests for comment. China's Foreign Ministry was closed for holidays, according to reports.The Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office in the United States also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Why Taiwan's president is a target for BeijingThe allegations come as relations between China and Taiwan remain deeply strained.Taiwan and China have been governed separately since the end of a civil war in 1949. Beijing claims sovereignty over the island and has repeatedly threatened to use force if necessary to prevent what it considers a formal separation of Taiwan from China.Lai, who was elected president in 2024, has repeatedly rejected Beijing's sovereignty claims over Taiwan. He has said that Taiwan and China do not belong to each other and that the “People's Republic of China has no right to represent Taiwan.”Beijing considers Lai a separatist and has accused him of being a “destroyer of peace”.Lai's Democratic Progressive Party supports Taiwan's separate political identity, a position that has frequently drawn strong criticism from Beijing.Since taking office, Lai has also sought to strengthen Taiwan's defence capabilities. He has pledged to raise defence spending from 3% to 5% of GDP and has pushed a special budget for construction of the T-Dome air defence system.US-China tensions add to espionage concernsThe arrest also highlights Washington's broader concerns about Chinese intelligence operations and alleged efforts to monitor people connected to Taiwan while they are in the United States.Although the United States does not maintain formal diplomatic relations with Taiwan, Washington is Taipei's most important international supporter and its main source of military equipment.The FBI has not alleged that Zhang was a Chinese government employee, but prosecutors say she acted at the direction of Chinese officials and failed to disclose her relationship with a foreign government.The case is now set to move before a federal court in Los Angeles, where Zhang is expected to face the charges brought against her.You use AI every day. articles.title: Army seeks to counter IEDs by procuring modern bomb detectors & 13 containment vehicles
articles.summary: The Army has set in motion a sweeping upgrade of its counter-Improvised Explosive Device (IED) and night-fighting capabilities, issuing requests for
articles.body: The Army has set in motion a sweeping upgrade of its counter-Improvised Explosive Device (IED) and night-fighting capabilities, issuing requests for information, which are expected at a later stage to lead to the procurement of 350 portable stand-off explosive detectors and 13 specialised bomb containment vehicles, as part of a coordinated push to modernise how frontline troops detect, neutralise and operate around explosive threats.IEDs have been used to target security forces in J&K, insurgency-affected areas of the North East and areas affected by Left-wing extremism.The explosive detectors, sought by the Army's Combat Engineers Directorate, are meant to identify trace and vapour residues from military, commercial and improvised explosive materials without requiring direct physical contact.These portable systems are expected to support personnel at checkpoints, critical installations and vehicle inspection points, as well as in field conditions.The devices are expected to give bomb disposal and counter-terror teams a faster, safer way to screen suspicious objects. They will need to run on battery power for a minimum of four hours continuously, with USB and Bluetooth connectivity built in for data transfer and for updating their explosive detection libraries as new threat signatures emerge.Alongside the detectors, the Army is also looking to acquire 13 total containment vehicles, specialised units designed to safely transport and, where necessary, neutralise explosive devices. These vehicles are required to allow liquid or vapour samples to be extracted through a vacuum-based system without any risk of external contamination, a critical requirement for preserving forensic evidence while keeping handling teams safe. These containment vehicles are designed in a manner that allows them to safely transport a bomb.In this case, the requirement states that the device should be able to carry an explosive with a blast effect equivalent to 8 kg of TNT, a common explosive used for benchmarking. The chamber is designed as what is called an "inside-out submarine", as it is meant to keep the massive shockwave, high-pressure gases and shrapnel inside the chamber, which is made from high-grade steel.These procurement threads reflect a broader, layered approach to force protection: systems to detect explosive threats before they cause harm, equipment to contain and dispose of them safely once found, and sensors to ensure troops retain the ability to spot and engage hostile movement regardless of lighting conditions or terrain. These procurements are expected to move forward through the self-reliance, or Atmanirbharta, route.

articles.title: After goats were removed in the 1990s and cats in 2001, Klein Curacao island restored native plants, helping nine bird species breed by 2022
articles.summary: Klein Curacao, a flat 130-hectare coral island about 10 km southeast of Curacao, was left bare by guano mining and overgrazing by goats and sheep.
articles.body: Klein Curacao, a flat 130-hectare coral island about 10 km southeast of Curacao, was left bare by guano mining and overgrazing by goats and sheep. Feral goats were removed in the 1990s and cats in October 2001, while native planting ran from 2000 to 2005. For decades, the Least Tern was the only seabird confirmed breeding there. According to the study published in ResearchGate, titled ‘A case study of sea and shorebird breeding recovery following goat and cat eradication on Klein Curacao, southern Caribbean’, surveys in 2021 and 2022 then confirmed eight further sea and shorebird species. Documented nesting rose from 140 pairs of a single species in 2002 to more than 430 pairs in 2021 and 650 pairs in 2022.How native plant restoration began on Klein Curacao in 2000Klein Curacao covers 130 hectares and lies roughly 10 km southeast of the main island of Curacao. The island is about 2.5 km long and about 700 m wide at its widest. Its maximum elevation is 4.7 m. Guano mining lowered and flattened it, and goats and sheep overgrazed it, leaving it devoid of bushes and trees for more than 100 years. Breeding boobies, once present, had disappeared by the early twentieth century because of egg harvesting, guano mining and grazing. Feral goats were removed in the 1990s. In July 2001, the vacant Least Tern colony was found littered with dead terns, and feral cats were eliminated by the Carmabi Foundation in October 2001.The Carmabi Foundation also assisted ecological recovery through replanting. Between 12 August 2000 and 16 November 2005, a total of 58 native plant species were taken from Curacao to Klein Curacao on 15-day trips. This comprised 1,174 individual saplings and potted plants, 482.7 kg of succulent cuttings, and 124.7 kg of seeds, fruits or cuttings of herbaceous plants. By mid-2022, the island's flora totalled approximately 54 species, of which 40 were surviving reintroductions, and many of these had been spreading naturally, producing landscape-level changes. The island was designated an Important Bird Area in 2008 and a Ramsar wetland in 2018.How weekly bird surveys were carried out in 2021 and 2022Weekly avifaunal assessments were carried out on Klein Curacao from January to December in both 2021 and 2022. Rob Wellens and Henriette de Vries, who were occasionally accompanied by other co-authors. All significant sightings and photographs were submitted to the eBird.org database. Survey timing depended on the sailing schedule of the touring vessel Mermaid, and visits generally took place between 9:30 am and 2:00 pm. During the height of the 2021 breeding season, Wellens stayed overnight once a week for three months, from July to September, to monitor birds and rat activity at night and at dusk.Bushnell trail cameras were used to monitor nesting by the Laughing Gull, Cayenne Tern and Least Tern. Sooty Terns and Bridled Terns were also monitored, as both are often most active at their nests at dusk or at night. In 2022, GPS coordinates were recorded for key locations to allow additional documentation. The authors report that the nine species were documented nesting across the island in 2021 and 2022, and that most nesting activity took place on the northern half of the island. The southern part was used almost exclusively by the Least Tern, and the single documented Green Heron nesting also took place there.Which seabird species became dominant on Klein CuracaoThe Cayenne Tern, Laughing Gull, Sooty Tern and Least Tern were the dominant species, in that order. The Cayenne Tern had approximately 230 breeding pairs in 2021 and 500 in 2022, and the authors note it had not been documented nesting on Klein Curacao since the 1960s. The Laughing Gull bred in both years with approximately 75 pairs; the study states this is the first confirmation of its breeding on the island, although it had long been suspected. Sooty Terns increased from 9 pairs in 2021 to between 40 and 45 pairs in 2022. The Least Tern colony was approximately 35 pairs in both years, compared with slightly more than 140 pairs recorded in 2002. The other four species had only a few nesting pairs each.Breeding by the Sooty Tern and the Bridled Tern are new national records for Curacao. In 2022, a Sooty Tern nest with a chick was confirmed on 13 July, and the first Bridled Tern chick was observed on 18 August. A Roseate Tern nest with one egg was found on 18 May 2022, and its fledgling was last seen near the nest on 20 July. The authors report the first nest of Common Terns, with two eggs, on 18 May 2022. They describe the American Oystercatcher as the first confirmed breeding for the territory of Curacao, with one pair in 2021 and two pairs in 2022. Green Heron breeding had never before been documented on Klein Curacao. According to the authors, the island is now the island group's most diverse and active seabird breeding location.What are the three major threats to seabird recovery on Klein CuracaoThree major threats to recovery: growing uncontrolled human recreation, the repeated threat of cat reintroduction and rat predation. On rats, the authors report that trail cameras recorded them in the breeding areas at night. In 2021, rats took Cayenne Tern eggs the night after they were laid, and all monitored nests lost their eggs. The authors state that rat predation appears to be less of a threat to the large, densely nesting Cayenne Tern than to smaller, less gregarious species. Starting in 2022, rat poison in the form of Klerat wax blocks containing 0.005% brodifacoum was deployed at selected tern nests. The authors urge at least seasonal rat control by poisoning during the tern breeding season, and recommend that rat removal be pursued as a priority.On cats and visitors, the authors credit the increase in abundance and diversity of nesting principally to the removal of cats. They cite Hughes et al. (2008), who found that around 100 cats on Ascension Island killed adult Sooty Terns at an average rate of 33 individuals a night in large breeding colonies. As of 2019, a single recently introduced house cat was present on Klein Curacao, and the authors state that the absence of cats at large must be guaranteed. They also report that the island receives more than 600 recreational day visitors a week. To limit disturbance, they recommend signage, a ban on unleashed pets, closure of the northern half of the island except with designated seabird guides, and cooperation from tour operators.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Texas man used this Civil War relic as a paperweight for years; bomb experts later found it was actually a live explosive
articles.summary: A Texas man kept a Civil War-era artillery shell on his desk for years, believing it was nothing more than a harmless dummy round.
articles.body: A Texas man kept a Civil War-era artillery shell on his desk for years, believing it was nothing more than a harmless dummy round. The object had become a conversation piece in his home, with visitors regularly picking it up and examining it. That changed after a man with military experience saw the relic and warned that it could still be live. The owner then contacted the Atascosa County Sheriff's Office, which brought in an explosive ordnance disposal team from Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland. Experts examined the roughly 20-pound object and identified it as a live Parrott round. It was later transported to an explosives range at Camp Bullis, where specialists safely destroyed it.How a Texas man turned a Civil War relic into a paperweightThe man, identified as Steve Martin, had acquired the object from his son, who had found it while fishing. Martin believed it was a dummy projectile and eventually began using it as a paperweight at his home in Atascosa County. For years, the unusual object attracted the attention of visitors, who would pick it up and look at it. Martin said he and others assumed it was some type of inert military display item. That belief remained unchanged until a truck driver with a military background visited and examined the object. The visitor became concerned that its appearance was consistent with a genuine artillery projectile and warned Martin that it might still contain an explosive charge.Experts identified it as a live Parrott roundAfter receiving the warning, Martin contacted the Atascosa County Sheriff's Office and reported that he might have a live Civil War-era explosive. Deputies arranged for an explosive ordnance disposal team from Joint Base San Antonio-Lackland to examine the object. Specialists confirmed that it was a live Parrott round, meaning the projectile was still capable of functioning as an explosive weapon despite being more than 160 years old. The discovery prompted authorities to treat the object as hazardous rather than as an ordinary historical artefact. Officials said no one was injured during the response and no charges were pending. The round was subsequently taken to Camp Bullis, a military training area and firing range north of San Antonio, for safe disposal.The shell was designed for a powerful Civil War cannonThe projectile was made for the Parrott rifle, a muzzle-loading rifled cannon developed by Robert Parker Parrott, a West Point graduate and inventor who became superintendent of the West Point Foundry. Parrott developed his rifled cannon system in the years immediately before the Civil War, with the first US rifled cannon of the design perfected in 1861. The weapon was recognisable by the wrought-iron reinforcing band around the rear of the gun, where pressures were greatest when it was fired. Parrott rifles were produced in several sizes and were used extensively by Union forces. The National Park Service records their use against Confederate-held Fort Pulaski in 1862 and Fort Sumter from 1863 to 1864.Parrott rifles changed Civil War artilleryThe Parrott system was significant because rifling gave artillery projectiles greater stability and accuracy than many earlier smoothbore weapons. Parrott also developed elongated projectiles designed specifically for his rifled guns. The combination allowed Union artillerymen to engage targets at greater distances and attack fortifications that had previously been difficult to damage. At Fort Pulaski, for example, Union forces used rifled artillery during the 1862 bombardment, helping demonstrate the vulnerability of traditional masonry fortifications to the newer technology. The National Park Service also records Parrott rifles among the artillery used during major Civil War operations, including the fighting around Antietam and the bombardment of Fort Sumter. The weapons became an important part of the Union's artillery arsenal during the conflict.The 160-year-old explosive was finally destroyedAfter specialists confirmed the Texas relic was live, they transported it to an explosives range at Camp Bullis rather than attempting to preserve it as a historical object. The round was safely detonated there, bringing an unexpected end to an object that had survived from the Civil War into the modern era. Martin reportedly regretted that the relic could not be kept, but the incident changed how he viewed unusual military artefacts. The discovery also illustrates why apparently old battlefield ammunition can remain a serious hazard long after the conflict in which it was manufactured. Similar Civil War-era shells have been found in Maryland and at Gettysburg National Military Park, where bomb technicians have also safely destroyed unexploded ammunition. For Martin, what had seemed like an ordinary paperweight turned out to be a live piece of Civil War ordnance sitting in his home for years.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor takes legal action over search warrants before his arrest
articles.summary: Mountbatten-Windsor's lawyers are challenging warrants used relating to his arrest in February on suspicion of misconduct in public office.
articles.body:
Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor is taking legal action against Thames Valley Police over his arrest in February.

The former Prince Andrew was arrested on suspicion of misconduct in public office , in the wake of information that emerged from the Epstein files in the United States.

Mountbatten-Windsor's lawyers are challenging the search warrants used in Sandringham and at Royal Lodge in Windsor relating to his arrest, as first reported by the Telegraph.

Thames Valley Police confirmed: "We are engaged in legal proceedings in relation to warrants previously obtained from the Central Criminal Court."

Why was Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor arrested and what happens next?

How Andrew's 11-hour detention on his birthday played out

Haunted photo of Andrew will be part of how arrest is remembered

"As these legal proceedings are currently ongoing, it would be inappropriate for us to comment further," a spokesperson for the force that carried out the arrest said.

Mountbatten-Windsor, who lost his titles as a prince and Duke of York over his connections to the sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, wants a judicial review to consider the legality of the search warrants.

A court hearing will be held on Thursday afternoon to begin considering this bid to quash the warrants, with the hearing set to begin in private. The judge will initially hear a request by the police to keep some documents private.

The warrants had been issued by a judge at the Central Criminal Court on 18 February - the day before Mountbatten-Windsor had been arrested - and the legal challenge is against the chief constable of Thames Valley Police and the Central Criminal Court.

"Even if Andrew succeeds in having the search warrants quashed, that would not necessarily be the victory it might first appear," said Nick Vamos, a criminal lawyer at Peters & Peters and former head of special crime at the Crown Prosecution Service.

Vamos said such disputes over warrants were not uncommon - but if the police lost on a technical error, they could still sometimes keep what they had obtained in a search.

"The police can apply back to the Crown Court to retain the material if they have grounds to immediately seize it again," said Vamos.

It would need to be a more fundamental issue with the granting of the warrants for the police to be required to return the material from a search, he said.

For several days after the arrest, police were seen searching Mountbatten-Windsor's property at Marsh Farm in Sandringham and at his former home, Royal Lodge, on the Windsor estate.

The arrest, carried out on his 66th birthday, followed a series of revelations from the Epstein files, published by the US Department of Justice.

They included emails appearing to show official documents being shared by Mountbatten-Windsor with Epstein and others, at a time when he was the UK's trade envoy.

Mountbatten-Windsor had already been stripped of his titles by King Charles, after emails had shown Mountbatten-Windsor had continued his links with Epstein, beyond when he had publicly said those links had been severed.

After Mountbatten-Windsor's arrest in February he was taken to Aylsham police station. A photograph captured his departure later that day, looking exhausted, after he was released under investigation.

The launch of this legal action against the police over the search warrants is the first public pushback from the former prince, who has lost his home, titles and public status, with charities and businesses distancing themselves from him.

Thames Valley Police says its investigation into Mountbatten-Windsor is continuing.

In a previous update it said the force had been "working with the United States Department of Justice to get further information that may be related to this investigation".

Detectives also highlighted that allegations of sexual misconduct could be considered as part of this inquiry into potential misconduct in public office.

Mountbatten-Windsor has consistently denied any wrongdoing in his associations with Epstein.
